question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the NAS and NFS concepts from the left onto the definitions on the right.
bank: Data storage and file sharing requests are sent and received.
The protocol is regularly used on Linux and UNIX systems.
Software is deployed on a lightweight OS that is embedded in the hardware.
The vendor-agnostic protocol is supported on any hardware and OS.
theory: NFS is a vendor-neutral, IETF-standardized protocol heavily associated with Linux/UNIX systems that simply defines how storage/file-sharing requests are exchanged between a client and server, while NAS refers to a purpose-built storage appliance running its own lightweight, embedded operating system on simplified hardware to serve that data. Keeping the protocol (NFS, which any OS/vendor can implement) distinct from the appliance/device concept (NAS, a dedicated hardware-plus-software storage platform) is the core distinction this match question tests. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 10 - NFS and NAS Concepts)
